title: Credential exposure scoring, per-scope TTLs, and emergency revoke flow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We need a unified admin and runtime strategy to reduce the blast radius of leaked API credentials while keeping developer UX reasonable. Current gaps: no exposure scoring to prioritize rotation, inconsistent enforcement of per-scope TTLs across hosted and dedicated, and a slow emergency revoke process requiring multi-step manual ops. This ticket designs and implements: 1) an exposure scoring signal fed from audit logs and usage anomalies to classify keys for urgent rotation; 2) enforceable per-scope TTLs with grace periods and automated reminder/remediation; 3) an emergency revocation fast-path with safe fallback and audit enrichment; 4) telemetry dashboards to measure rotation latency, key reuse, and post-rotation failure rates.
acceptance_criteria: Exposure scoring prototype runs in prod pipeline and annotates keys in the credential catalog with low/medium/high exposure tags
Per-scope TTLs enforced consistently: tokens created with a scope TTL are auto-expired by the token service after TTL + configurable grace period
Console admin UI shows exposure score, last-use, risk factors, and a one-click emergency revoke that triggers immediate revoke + rolling fallback to emergency token for dependent services
Audit logs record exposure score at revoke/create/change events and include actor, request id, affected resources, and pre/post token state
Dashboard dashboards: 7-day rotation latency, percent of high-exposure tokens rotated within SLA, and post-rotation 5xx/unauthenticated spike metric (<= 2% regression threshold)
tasks: Design exposure scoring model (weight audit anomalies, geo mismatch, sudden spike in token use, token age, reuse across services)
Implement scoring pipeline: audit-log consumer -> enrichment -> credential catalog annotation
Add per-scope TTL enforcement in token service and credential lifecycle worker
Build graceful expiration: configurable grace window, notification emails/console banners, automated short-lived fallback tokens for services with pinned credentials
Emergency revoke API: endpoint + audit-safe orchestration that can trigger fallback model and notify on-call
Console changes: admin table column for exposure score + revoke button + TTL editor
Telemetry: Grafana dashboard + alert rule for high exposure rate and failed rollouts after automated rotation
E2E tests and canary rollout for dedicated/private deployments where on-prem TTL enforcement differs
